enAudit: habitats G1-398, G1-406, G2-380 instructions are TWO sentences and G2-381 is THREE; cursive G2-386 and G3-401 are two. The brief requires one child-level sentence; es authors each as one sentence.
sink-or-float G2-382 "Color where each clay shape ends up" never names what is coloured (a ring in each tank); es names it: "Colorea en cada pecera el círculo donde queda...".
sink-or-float G1-408 EN title capitalises "With" mid-title ("...Experiment With a Scale"), inconsistent with the title-case of its siblings ("a Change the Shape Experiment").
healthy-habits reason brush-teeth "It keeps holes away": "holes" for cavities reads as holes in the teeth being kept out, ambiguous at G2; es uses the school word "caries".

healthy-habits G1-405 EN title "Healthy Habits Chart" is fine, but the rail head "Hygiene" does not describe three of its five rows (move, drink water, sleep); es titles F5 "higiene, ejercicio y descanso" and F4 "higiene y salud" so the title names what is on the page.
story beach-walk: the EN "a child" becomes a gendered noun in Spanish (niña/niño); the walker is faceless, so any choice is arbitrary. es picks "una niña"; flag for the other gendered locales.

sink-or-float es: the vocab lemon is a YELLOW lemon; in Mexico "limón" is the green lime. The label stays "limón" ("limón amarillo" does not fit the 96 px tile) and is not a truth problem (both float); cursive drops fruits/lemon from the es word list for the same reason.

habitats es strand: the live Science row renders es "Conocimiento del Medio", a SPAIN subject name (OPEN 1). The Mexican NEM term is the campo formativo "Saberes y pensamiento científico"; changing it is catalogue-wide, not a panel edit.
